    Free Spins vs Bonus Spins: Spot the Differences

    I noticed some of your fellow players getting confused when casino operators change the way they present their free spins offers using words like "bonus" or "extra." Such a change may be strategic, but in many cases, it’s compliance-related.

    It is my duty to explain the core differences between these two and how to position yourself when claiming free or bonus spins.

    Free Spins

    • When the bonus requirements do not include a deposit obligation, the rotations are really free from a financial standpoint.

    • These spins tend to come as standalone offers that simply promote the batch of free casino spins.

    • In rarer cases, these are part of a promotion that contains other perks, too. 

    Bonus Spins

    • I see these offered as an extra perk, with the main bonus usually a deposit match.

    • The majority of online operators use "bonus spins" as a synonym for "free spins". It’s a method of signalling that you can get these rotations after depositing.

    • Sometimes, casinos add separate deposits for the bonus spins, too. 

    • I’ve encountered plenty of examples in which a deposit is exclusively linked to the free spins reward.

    Such details are always in the terms and conditions in some capacity, which is always beneficial. You just need to be directly attentive towards them and read them carefully!

    Short Free Spins Incentives Dictionary

    I want to give you a consistent list of bonus types for free spins. But before that, I want to make sure you completely understand all the industry terminology.

    I am using some gambling-specific terms to keep things consistent with real-life situations that you will encounter when playing online. Casinos use them regularly, so it's in your best interest to make sure you understand their meaning.

    • No deposit rounds: Video slot machine spins that you can receive for free, with no additional obligations to deposit.

    • Deposit free spins: Rotations that you will receive after making a deposit. In most of today’s cases, they carry the ‘bonus’ or ‘extra’ spins monikers.

    • Wagering requirements: The number of times you must wager winnings from free rounds before you are able to withdraw.

    • Maximum cashout cap: A limit on the amount you’re able to withdraw as personal winnings from free spins. If the cap is $50, that’s the maximum amount that you’ll receive into your account.

    • Game availability: A directive that will tell you which slots you can play with a specific set of costless rotations.

    • Spin value: Each free spin bonus comes with a fixed value limit for each rotation. Most of the offers that I’ve assessed are at circa $0.1.

    • Bonus code: A specific combination of letters, symbols, and numbers that you may use as a key to unlock certain free spin incentives.

    • RTP: The Return To Player metric is usually expressed as a percentage that indicates how efficient a slot machine is. For instance, the game is programmed to return 98% of the money you’ve invested in it. It does not mean that you will receive 98% of your money back.

    Will Free Offers Lead to Gambling Problems?

    Gambling addiction is one of the top ten addictions in the world based on the number of people who develop it internationally. The danger is real, and like any other addiction, it will always start as a fun experience. 

    To understand if free offers really lead to gambling problems, you have to understand how addiction develops as an affliction. 

    The biological mechanism behind it is pretty simple and carries the following sequence:

    • When we take risks, our brains release several substances, including dopamine. It is responsible for the thrilling sensation we feel at each round.

    • If, after a big risk like a financial bet, you end up winning, you feel happiness. This combination of thrill, enthusiasm, and happiness leads to addiction.

    • The more you play, the more your brain gets used to it, which leads to you taking much higher risks, usually translating to bigger, more reckless bets.

    Can free offers sustain the development of gambling addiction? 

    Yes, but not by default, because responsible gambling can help you avoid unwanted situations.

    If you are a beginner and your first contact with gambling is through a free offer that leads to big winnings, it’s undoubtedly dangerous to consider that gambling is a guaranteed source of income. 

    My Top Advice On How To Avoid Addiction

    You have to respect some basic, responsible gambling rules. They will only be in your best interest, not to mention your long-term satisfaction.

    1. Placing bets should be a relaxing activity that you enjoy with a clear head and a light heart. Gambling is not a safe or reliable source of income. 

    2. Set a spending limit to set sensible parameters for your gaming experience.

    3. Betting money you cannot afford to lose is a dangerous proposition since financial security is always more important.

    4. Learn to ration your bets properly so you can have a more sustainable gaming experience. Do not spend too much time in a betting session. 

    5. Always be aware of the fact that casinos are businesses and have a guaranteed house edge.

    6. If gambling affects you emotionally, you have to stop and recalibrate your mental state if you are to ever return to games of luck!

    Key Expert Note: A good practice I personally use and can recommend is to reduce the intensity of my sessions by taking advantage of a free bonus. It does not involve risking my own cash, giving me more flexibility by lowering the stakes of said gaming experience.
